title: Interval Tree: Count Overlapping Intervals
statement:
You are given N intervals [l, r] and Q query points. For each query point p, count how many intervals contain p (i.e., l <= p <= r).

An efficient approach is to use an interval tree or a coordinate-compressed BIT/sweep.

Print the count for each query on a separate line.
inputFormat:
The first line contains N.
The next N lines each contain two integers l and r.
The next line contains Q.
The next Q lines each contain a query point p.
outputFormat: Q lines, each the count of intervals that contain the query point.
